item.title: Accor’s Message to Sofitel Owners: ‘Renovate, Rebrand, or Exit’
item.description: Accor, the Paris-based hospitality company, is continuing a sweeping renovation campaign at Sofitel, its largest luxury hotel brand.

item.title: American Airlines Unions Escalate Pressure on CEO After Storm Failures and Weak Profits
item.description: American’s weak earnings means less profit-sharing for employees — and unions are losing patience.

item.title: The 2026 Winter Olympics Are an Endurance Test for Travelers, Not Just Athletes
item.description: Milano Cortina 2026 is testing whether modern mega-events can function without a single dominant transport hub.

item.title: MGM Resorts’ Las Vegas Revenue Dropped, But CEO Says Worst Is Over
item.description: MGM Resorts said Las Vegas is stabilizing after a tourism decline last year, though leisure travel and Canadian visits remain soft.

item.title: Prism-Backed Asset Arm Acquires 8 Hotels in Upmarket Push
item.description: Sunday PropTech expansion shows Prism’s effort to shed its budget-hotel image ahead of an IPO and present a more predictable business to investors.

item.title: A Remote Atoll and the Economics of Ultra-Luxury Conservation
item.description: Tetiaroa proves that conservation works when it's designed as architecture: binding governance and indigenous knowledge made operational. It's a useful source code for other climate-sensitive areas.

item.title: Choice Hotels Targets 100 Hotels in Africa by 2035
item.description: Choice must prove its partner-led, franchise-only model can overcome a regional track record of slow builds and unrealized projects.

item.title: Jet Fuel Made From Sewage Draws Airline Interest
item.description: The real test is whether this long-studied technology that converts waste into oil can clear certification and financing fast enough to make a dent before mandates start pushing airfares higher.

item.title: Flyadeal to Squeeze More Flying From its Fleet to Fuel Expansion
item.description: Flyadeal's CEO believes the airline has seen the worst of the aircraft delivery delays, but engine reliability and spare parts shortages remain a concern.

item.title: Activists Target Hilton CEO’s Home Over ICE Housing
item.description: Targeting a CEO’s home marks a new phase in the anti-ICE campaign — and a reminder that hotel groups now face reputational risks in an ever-more politicized moment.
